old_caption: The video showcases a Sony 5 CD Changer Disc Exchange System on a white surface. The device is black with a digital display showing "d 15C - 1" and various control buttons. Two CDs are visible inside the open front panel: one labeled "NatureScapes" and the other "The Beatles." A hand enters from the right and presses the "OPEN/CLOSE" button, but the panel remains open. The hand then presses another button, and the CDs stay stationary. The background remains consistent, focusing on the CD changer and the hand interacting with it.
original_wisa_caption: The video showcases a Sony 5 CD Changer Disc Exchange System placed on a white surface. The device is black with a digital display showing "d 15C - 1" and various buttons for functions such as play, stop, fast forward, and reverse. A hand appears from the right side of the frame, pressing the "OPEN/CLOSE" button, which causes the front panel to open. Inside, two CDs are visible: one labeled "NatureScapes" and the other "The Beatles." The hand then presses another button, likely to start the disc changer, as the CDs begin to rotate. The video captures the mechanical movement of the discs as they spin, highlighting the functionality of the device. The background remains consistent throughout, focusing solely on the CD changer and the hand interacting with it.
caption: The video showcases a black Sony 5-disc CD changer resting on a white surface with a sheet of paper on top, its disc tray fully extended to hold two CDs side by side. The front display reads DISC-1 throughout the excerpt. On the tray, a silver disc labeled NATURESCAPES sits on the left and a black disc labeled Beatles on the right. During the opening moments both discs turn through a small angle, shifting the rainbow diffraction pattern across the silver surface, after which they settle and remain still for the middle of the clip. Near the end a person's finger enters from the right edge and rests on the control buttons along the right side. The tray stays open and no further mechanical motion is visible as the hand holds contact through the final frame.
